words.sense: Young person with extraordinary ability far beyond their age
misconceptions: Assuming every gifted child has a mentor.
Assuming mentoring proves exceptional natural talent.

words.sense: Person receiving guidance and backing from a mentor
misconceptions: Assuming every gifted child has a mentor.
Treating an award as evidence of an ongoing mentor relationship.

semantic_axes.description: Prodigy identifies exceptional ability at a young age; protégé identifies a person selected for ongoing guidance or support by a mentor.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Aya as a pianist?

beats.text: At twelve, Aya plays a difficult concert piece flawlessly after hearing it just once.
beats.reason: The initial evidence is extraordinary skill demonstrated at twelve; it best supports prodigy.

beats.text: Experienced musicians ask her to demonstrate how she learned it so quickly.
beats.decisive_clue: exceptional performance at an unusually young age
beats.reason: The reaction adds context to the extraordinary ability already shown.

chains.feedback_short: The reaction adds context to the extraordinary ability already shown.
chains.feedback_deep: Prodigy means exceptionally gifted young person; protégé means mentee under the care of an established supporter. The reaction adds context to the extraordinary ability already shown.
chains.contrast_rule: A prodigy amazes through youthful skill; a protégé grows under a mentor.
